A parallel Fortran framework for neural networks and deep learning
. It loads the library’s MNIST files, trains a dense classifier for 10 epochs, and prints validation accuracy, a quadratic loss, and a Pearson correlation.

program dense_mnist

  use nf, only: dense, input, network, sgd, label_digits, load_mnist, corr, relu, softmax, dropout

  implicit none

  type(network) :: net
  real, allocatable :: training_images(:,:), training_labels(:)
  real, allocatable :: validation_images(:,:), validation_labels(:)
  integer :: n, num_epochs

  call load_mnist(training_images, training_labels, &
                  validation_images, validation_labels)

  print '("MNIST")'
  print '(60("="))'

  net = network([ &
    input(784), &
    dense(64, relu()), &
    dropout(0.2), &
    dense(10, softmax()) &
  ])
  num_epochs = 10

  call net % print_info()

  print '(a,f5.2,a)', 'Initial accuracy: ', accuracy( &
    net, validation_images, label_digits(validation_labels)) * 100, ' %'

from the neural-fortran file store and unpacks it. This run found the files already unpacked in the working directory. The counts in the loader are 50000 training images, 10000 validation images, and 10000 test images. This program does not request the test arrays.
Each image is 784 floats, one per pixel, stored as a column.

      training_images, &

    end block

contains

  real function accuracy(net, x, y)
    type(network), intent(in out) :: net
    real, intent(in) :: x(:,:), y(:,:)
    integer :: i, good
    good = 0
    do i = 1, size(x, dim=2)
      if (all(maxloc(net % predict(x(:,i))) == maxloc(y(:,i)))) then
        good = good + 1
      end if
    end do
    accuracy = real(good) / size(x, dim=2)
  end function accuracy

steps. Each step draws a random contiguous window of 128 images. Windows can overlap, and an image can be skipped. The window is not a shuffled partition of the dataset.
divides the accumulated gradient by the batch size before the SGD step, so the learning rate multiplies the mean gradient of the window.

children.value: The reduction in the program is

loops the first dimension. The mean is therefore the mean of 10 class-channel scores, and each channel score is computed across all 10000 validation images. The printed loss is not a per-image average. A per-image quadratic loss on a softmax would sit below 1. The values near 20 are sums over the validation set, averaged across the ten digit channels. The Pearson number is the same kind of average, which is why it can sit near 0.97 next to a loss near 22.

program dense_mnist

  use nf, only: dense, input, network, sgd, label_digits, load_mnist, corr, relu, softmax, dropout

  implicit none

  type(network) :: net
  real, allocatable :: training_images(:,:), training_labels(:)
  real, allocatable :: validation_images(:,:), validation_labels(:)
  integer :: n, num_epochs

  call load_mnist(training_images, training_labels, &
                  validation_images, validation_labels)

  print '("MNIST")'
  print '(60("="))'

  net = network([ &
    input(784), &
    dense(64, relu()), &
    dropout(0.2), &
    dense(10, softmax()) &
  ])
  num_epochs = 10

  call net % print_info()

  print '(a,f5.2,a)', 'Initial accuracy: ', accuracy( &
    net, validation_images, label_digits(validation_labels)) * 100, ' %'

  epochs: do n = 1, num_epochs

    call net % train( &
      training_images, &
      label_digits(training_labels), &
      batch_size=128, &
      epochs=1, &
      optimizer=sgd(learning_rate=3.) &
    )

    block
      real, allocatable :: output_metrics(:,:)
      real, allocatable :: mean_metrics(:)
      ! 2 metrics; 1st is default loss function (quadratic), other is Pearson corr.
      output_metrics = net % evaluate(validation_images, label_digits(validation_labels), metric=corr())
      mean_metrics = sum(output_metrics, 1) / size(output_metrics, 1)
      print '(a,i2,3(a,f6.3))', 'Epoch ', n, ' done, Accuracy: ', &
        accuracy(net, validation_images, label_digits(validation_labels)) * 100, &
        '%, Loss: ', mean_metrics(1), ', Pearson correlation: ', mean_metrics(2)
    end block

  end do epochs

contains

  real function accuracy(net, x, y)
    type(network), intent(in out) :: net
    real, intent(in) :: x(:,:), y(:,:)
    integer :: i, good
    good = 0
    do i = 1, size(x, dim=2)
      if (all(maxloc(net % predict(x(:,i))) == maxloc(y(:,i)))) then
        good = good + 1
      end if
    end do
    accuracy = real(good) / size(x, dim=2)
  end function accuracy

end program dense_mnist
The package file below builds this source with fpm. The Fortran program itself is the file from the repository.

name = "Section_Examples_Dense_Mnist"

[build]
auto-executables = true
auto-tests = true
auto-examples = true

[install]
library = false

[dependencies]
neural-fortran = { git = "https://github.com/modern-fortran/neural-fortran.git" }

[[executable]]
name = "Section_Examples_Dense_Mnist"
source-dir = "app"
main = "dense_mnist.f90"

Before any update the validation accuracy is 5.99 percent, which is 599 of 10000 images. An untrained network does not have to land near the 10 percent chance line.

Epoch 10 is 9700 of 10000 validation images. The printed loss dips and then rises slightly from epoch 6 to epoch 7 while accuracy stays flat. Epoch 9 is a hair above epoch 10 in accuracy. The program does not evaluate the separate test file.
The training call is one subroutine,
loop. The accuracy function is ordinary Fortran around
. The loss column needs the shape note above before it is compared with a per-image mean squared error.
